title: Six rows from OpenAI’s xhigh table
intro: Move across six models from the xhigh table in OpenAI’s 6 November 2026 BioBasicsBench post. Each stop is that model’s mean, the interval the post prints beside it, and the output tokens per task. The page does not subtract the scores, and it does not turn a percent into a lab sign-off.
note: Every figure on the control is from the xhigh table in OpenAI’s post “Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science,” dated 6 November 2026. Xhigh is the highest reasoning setting the post reports for all seven models. Each row is all 100 tasks and five attempts. Mean reward is the average task score as a percentage of the available credit. The intervals are the post’s 95 percent confidence intervals. The token counts are output tokens per task. The post’s seventh xhigh row is not on this control: GPT-5.2 at 31.2 percent, interval 26.2 to 36.3 percent, 27,620 output tokens. The post says the whole evaluation is 37 settings and 18,500 results. This control does not show the other effort settings. The post’s comparison sentence is GPT-6 Astra at 66.7 percent against GPT-5.6 Sol at 43.8 percent. It also prints GPT-6.1 Sol at 62.0 percent. This control does not test whether two intervals overlap. The approximately 12 percent colony overcount is a different passage, about one plate, and it is not a row here. The post says a higher score is not yet a reliable judgment in the lab.
